    • v3.5.0 · 📊 Puzzle-Data Refresh — #135 SOLVED 2026-07-28 — RetiredCoder, Pollard Kangaroo, ~5 months on ~200 GPUs. Sweep tx 817535430c600810080662dd425a2e335f771effd950d28fc443bce4a92fa812, block 959946. Published key 0000000000000000000000000000006d9392a16883f90903d5f78da57af07eb2 (verified: derives the file's pubkey / hash160 / address exactly). Counts 82→83 solved / 78→77 unsolved, exposed 6→5 (#140, #145, #150, #155, #160), nominal prize 916.5→903.0 BTC, exposed prize 88.5→75.0 BTC. #140 is now the lowest unsolved pubkey-exposed target. Data sync stamp 2026-11-08. Sources: Mathricks, OnePiece-Bitcoin (verified on-chain 2026-08-20), puzzles.agntn.dev, lotterypuzzle.org, dec0ded.tech.
    • v3.5.0 · ⚡ Engine P0 — correctness + persistence, not another strategy pack — Kangaroo: DP store capped at 250,000 entries (LRU), walk checkpoint saved to OPFS (bphks_kangaroo_v1.json) and resumed via cfg.kangarooResume, hard-abort when a Kangaroo/BSGS puzzle has no pubkey (no more silent dual-scalar no-op). BSGS: table bits capped at T≤24, RAM table corrected to measured JS Map costs (T=20 ≈100 MB, T=24 ≈1.5–2 GB, T=26 refused), pre-flight refusal when span/2^T > 2^26, giant-step counter now counts giant steps (not STEP keys), BSGS added to xpoint6 mode. Progress: 5 s OPFS save now includes per-worker cursors, Kangaroo DP count and coverage-dirty state; resume restores them. Workers: capped to cores−1 (3 on a 4-core VM) — desktop/balanced presets updated, turbo labelled oversubscribing. NOT implemented (see changelog): multi-herd Kangaroo, shared/packed BSGS table, live pool-range fetch, 60 s benchmark, WebGPU kernel.
    • v3.5.0 · 🌐 Live Sync — verification gate, opt-in, fetch-only — Primary list: OnePiece-Bitcoin data/puzzles.json via raw.githubusercontent.com (verified 2026-11-08: object with counts{solved:83, unsolved:77} and puzzles[] of {n, type, keyspace, address, balance_btc, public_key, status}; n maps to bits, no min/max/h160 in the file — those come from the embedded data). Verifiers: mempool.space + blockstream.info Esplora (/api/address/:address). Rule: never auto-apply solved status — a change is staged in quarantine, checked on-chain on BOTH hosts, and only applied after the user clicks Apply per row. CSP connect-src adds only mempool.space + blockstream.info. No privatekeyfinder / privatekeys.pw / hashkeys / bitcointalk / Telegram fetch — those are link/format references only. Offline banner: "Offline — using embedded data (2026-07-28)".
    • v3.5.0 · 💬 Community — Telegram @bitcoin_keys link-out only — Link labelled "Community group (unverified tips — verify on-chain before trusting)" to https://t.me/bitcoin_keys, with the scam warning: never paste a seed phrase or private key anywhere, never pay for a puzzle key, verify any claimed solve on-chain (spending tx + derived address). The app makes no network request to Telegram and holds no bot token. Group posts are not web-accessible; tips are curated manually, verified on-chain, then committed as embedded data.
    v3.4.28 · 2026.06.15 · 3 entries ⚡
    • v3.4.28 · 🦞 Phase 88 — BUG-RA-INSIGHT-DETACHED-TR FIX · ST-829 (no version bump) — Fixes a console-flooding crash surfaced via a pasted device console log (hundreds of identical stack traces in a tight burst). BUG-RA-INSIGHT-DETACHED-TR (HIGH): _injectInsightRow(tr, hex) is invoked from two deferred requestIdleCallback sites — the KB Insight batch inside _kbRender and the Recent Attempts path inside _augmentRaRow — both queued with a {timeout: 300} fallback, meaning the callback can fire up to 300ms after the tr reference was captured. Under an active multi-puzzle scan, pushRecent() trims #recentBody down to MAX_RECENT via removeChild(recentBody.lastChild) on every push past the cap, and _kbRender() rebuilds #kbBody wholesale on re-render/page-navigation — both detach the original <tr> from the document well before the queued idle callback runs. The function's trailing tr.parentNode.insertBefore(insightTr, tr.nextSibling) then threw TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'insertBefore') on every fired callback against a stale row, flooding the console in a tight loop during fast scans. Fix: _injectInsightRow now bails out immediately — if (!tr || !tr.parentNode) return; — before any BigInt/APD/PIL/ACA/SVE insight-scoring computation runs, plus a defense-in-depth re-check of tr.parentNode immediately before the trailing insertBefore() call. Zero behavioural change for the common case (row still attached) and a meaningful perf win on the failure path, since the full insight-scoring pipeline (≈700 lines) is skipped entirely for a row about to be discarded. ST-829 new: source-pattern assertion that the detached-tr guard is present in _injectInsightRow.toString(), wired into the Phase 87 Audit Hardening Pack runner alongside ST-828. Self-test ceiling: ≈729+/ST-829. VersionGuard green (no bump). No changes to scan correctness, cryptographic workers, or insight-scoring math. — 🦞 claude.ai research · 🔬 zync · 🐉 dra69on · 👾 aoxy · 🦋 agnarez · ❤️‍🔥 0xindy · 🐇 0xfinu
    • v3.4.28 · 🦞 Phase 87 — Audit Response Pack: ST-821 · ST-822 · ST-823 (no version bump) — Three surgical patches landed in response to the chat audit pass. ST-821 — window.safeBigInt(val): new crash-safe BigInt coercion utility placed immediately after _b2hSafe in the BigInt-utility cluster. Three-branch logic — bigint passthrough → 0x-prefixed string → bare numeric/decimal/hex string — wrapped in try/catch with 0n fallback so boundary comparisons (zone in/out, advisory range, KITT/LK/All-Puzzles intel surfaces) never throw a TypeError on a mis-typed source. ST-822 — _addKittIntelOverlay rAF decoupling: the scanner:tick hot path no longer paints synchronously. New _rAFPending + _latestKittHex closure pair captures the latest hex per tick and drains it on the next requestAnimationFrame (with a setTimeout(16) fallback). _THROTTLE_MS dropped 500 → 300 ms since rAF is now the cadence gate — fewer dropped frames during heavy multi-puzzle scans, no behavioural regression. ST-823 — CWVG BroadcastChannel relay + #cwvgGateModePill: when SharedArrayBuffer is unavailable (most file:// sessions, missing COOP/COEP), worker FOUND signals previously had no cross-worker relay path. A same-origin BroadcastChannel('bphks-cwvg-v1') now mirrors the verdict; host cwvgSignalFound is wrapped to also broadcast, and inbound BC {t:'found',wi} messages mirror back into the SAB path via _nclLayer.cwvgSignalFound. New 🚦 CWVG pill inside #kittIntelOverlay surfaces the active transport: SAB (green) when the verdict buffer is shared, BC (amber) when BroadcastChannel is the relay, HOST (muted) when neither is available — closes the silent-fail UX gap identified in the audit. Diagnostics: window._nclLayer.cwvgGateMode(), cwvgBC, cwvgRelayFound, cwvgPillRefresh. ST-821/822/823 added; self-test ceiling: ≈728+/ST-828 (incl. ST-824→ST-828 Hardening Pack). BUG-TF-HIST-LAST (LOW): Batch 8 (the final batch of every Triple Fusion run) was silently dropped from the Batch History log. Root cause: _hookBatchCompletionObserver uses a MutationObserver on the status line, detecting transitions via /Batch\s+(\d+)\/(\d+)/ — it logs batch N when batch N+1 starts. But after batch 8, the status changes to "⏹ Stopped" (no batch pattern), so no transition fires and batch 8 statistics are permanently lost. Fix: observer now checks for "Stopped" or "Idle" text while _lastBatchN !== null; computes per-batch zone-width stats from getBatches()[_lastBatchN-1].zonesByBits, propagates to _tfMeta.zoneWidthStats, appends the entry via _batchLogAppend, then resets _lastBatchN = null to prevent duplicate entries if the scan is restarted.     • v3.4.17 · 🐛 Phase 53 — BUG-TF-ERRLOG FIX · ST-673 — Diagnostic blind-spot fix across all catch(e) + console.warn blocks. BUG-TF-ERRLOG (MEDIUM): 25 catch blocks throughout the codebase called console.warn(label, e) with a bare Error object as the second argument. JavaScript Error objects have non-enumerable own properties (message, stack, name); when serialised by mobile browsers (mobile Safari, Android Chrome, any DevTools-closed environment), the error appears as {} — a completely empty object with zero diagnostic value. The reported symptom "WARN [🌌⛏️ Triple Fusion] startHunt error: {}" is the canonical example: startHunt() was throwing an exception on every Triple Fusion batch launch, but the catch silently swallowed it, showing only {}. This created a silent CRITICAL regression class — the scan may never start while Triple Fusion shows a running UI state. Fix: all 25 occurrences changed from console.warn(label, e) → console.warn(label, String(e), e). String(e) always produces a human-readable message ("TypeError: Cannot read properties of null" etc.) in every environment. The trailing bare e is retained so desktop DevTools still shows the expandable Error object with full stack trace. Affected catch sites: [🌌⛏️ Triple Fusion] startHunt error · [🌌⛏️ Triple Fusion] ACA zone error · [ACA §O] startHunt error · [ACA §O] _acaComputeZone error · [3FSN Sync] patch error · [v3.1.8 post-boot patch] failed · all 19 self-test suite crash handlers ([APD-Learn tests] · [§I12 dashboard] · [APD-Learn v2.2.0 tests] · [BPH-tests] · [Heatmap/Adjacency/Corpus Persist/Corpus Mutate/Solve Injector/CommImport/CorpusVer/SessionReport/OnlineSync/TFOP tests] · [§I1–§I4 FFT/K-means/CRT/LLL tests] · [v3.4.12 intelligence tests]). ST-673 new: asserts String(e) is present alongside [🌌⛏️ Triple Fusion] startHunt error: and [ACA §O] startHunt error: catch blocks — the two highest-impact diagnostic sites. Result: scan permanently stuck, never actually starting. Fixed: guard now checks window._acaAutoScan.active; on re-entry from _acaApplyZoneAndHunt it resolves the strategy to 'segrand' and proceeds normally — window._acaZoneOverride supplies the correct ACA-computed zone. BUG-ACA-PICKER-3 (HIGH): _STRAT_MODE_MAP.xpoint6 did not include aca-nova / aca-top1 / aca-confweight / aca-combined. When _acaApplyZoneAndHunt set #mode='xpoint6' and dispatched a change event, the mode-change handler found aca-* ∉ xpoint6 validSet and silently forced stratSel.value='auto' — scanner then ran random auto strategy instead of ACA. Fixed: four aca-* IDs added to the xpoint6 Set. ST-643 new: verifies _acaOStart source contains typeof mode === 'string' guard (BUG-ACA-PICKER-1).     📝 Release Notes — v3.5.0 · 3FSN v3.5.0 Categories: 🆕 NEW FEATURE · 🔧 FIX · ⚡ PERF · 📝 DOCS · 🔄 REFACTOR

      RNG bias fix — _rnd(lo, span) previously used naive (rand & mask) % span, which produces modulo bias toward smaller values whenever span is not a power of two. Replaced with rejection sampling over the largest span-aligned window of 2²⁵⁶, yielding a perfectly uniform distribution across each puzzle's keyspace.

      Stats double-count fix — _jobStats.totalKeys was incrementing by the worker's full cumulative cnt on every TICK, inflating reported keys-tested by orders of magnitude. Now tracks the per-job last cnt and adds only the delta, so on-screen Keys/Speed match true throughput.

      Worker tick overhead reduced — TICK posts coalesced (only when cnt changed since last tick), TICK_MS raised to 120/180 ms tier, and the rng buffer enlarged to 4 KiB. Scan correctness for hash160 / address / xpoint membership checks is byte-identical to v1.0.9.

      Cryptographic audit pass — secp256k1 BigInt fallback, Jacobian add/double, batch inversion, SHA-256, RIPEMD-160, Base58Check and WIF (compressed) re-verified against published vectors.

      Offline verification mode (new) — deterministic test-vector replay via the 🛡 button; refuses to scan if any vector mismatches.

      Version metadata synced across <title>, brand sub-line, APP_VERSION, engine LOG banner, and Changelog tab.

    ⚡ Jump to Phase
    🌱 Phase 0 — Genesis v1.0.6 · 2026.04
    The original BPH KITT Scanner ships as a single HTML file. OMEGA V3.13.30 engine provides WASM-accelerated secp256k1 + RIPEMD-160 + batch inversion. Four known cryptographic test vectors validated on load. Supports hash160, address, and xpoint match modes. Dark/light/auto theming, localStorage state persistence, CSV/JSON/TXT hit export. Offline by design — zero network calls, zero trackers.
    ⚙️ Phase 1 — Engine & Infrastructure v1.1.0 – v1.3.2 · 2026.04–05
    Major rebase to OMEGA V3.13.30 — WASM SHA-256 fused path, SIMD detection, adaptive batch sizing, and batch inversion. Round-robin worker pool with heartbeat watchdog + auto-respawn. Tuning presets (Balanced · Mobile · Desktop · ⚡ Turbo) with live worker reconfig. Verbose/Turbo toggles. RNG rejection-sampling bias fix. Stats delta-tracking (no more double-count inflation). Haptic feedback via Web Vibration API (13 distinct tactile patterns). VersionGuard consistency banner across title / meta / JS constant / engine banner. 18 self-test assertions.
    🗺️ Phase 2 — Strategies & Coverage v1.4.0 – v1.6.0 · 2026.05
    Scan strategy system introduced: Auto · Random · Seg-Rand 1M-blocks · Epoch Cursor · LCG Sweep · Sequential · Stride · Walk · BSGS (Baby-Step Giant-Step) · Kangaroo (Pollard's Rho) · Gaussian weak-key proximity. Coverage map (localStorage bitfield) avoids re-scanning visited blocks. Auto-slice and range partition across workers for zero inter-worker overlap.     ⚡ DET-CHAIN ⛓ · BITWISE-MASK ⊞ · XOR-MUT ⊕ (Phase 76 · v3.4.24) — Three new multi-puzzle-only scan strategies (all-78 + xpoint6; single mode excluded via _STRAT_MODE_MAP guard + single-mode guard toast). DET-CHAIN ⛓: deterministic Armory/Electrum SHA-256 chain key derivation — k[i] = SHA256(pz_seed‖i_LE4) mod pz.span + pz.lo; per-puzzle seed via _dcPuzzleSeed(pz, dcRoot); canonical default root SHA256("BPHKS-DET-CHAIN-v1") = b7e2a3f1c94d650e…; Armory/Electrum compatible. BITWISE-MASK ⊞: three sub-modes — AND-mask sub-lattice (periodic structure via AND mask), XOR-flip Hamming neighborhood (Hamming-distance-1 bit-flip sweep), LSHIFT power-of-2 probe (bit-aligned targets). XOR-MUT ⊕: HW-capped mutation sweep — k = anchor XOR SHA256(nonce), capped to puzzle expected Hamming weight; CPAE auto-anchors to last CPAE zone if available. Common infrastructure: 3 hidden <option> elements in #strategy for picker routing · 3 _STRAT_META entries (label, scope, desc, statusHint) · _STRAT_MODE_MAP all + xpoint6 include all 3 (single set excluded) · startHunt() delegation blocks with single-mode guard toast · stopHunt() silent-stop cascade for all 3 engines · 3 engine IIFEs (_detChainScan / _bitmaskScan / _xorMutScan) each with autoScanStart / autoScanStop / autoScanSilentStop. 16 new self-tests ST-743→ST-758: ST-743 _detChainScan is function · ST-744 DET-CHAIN symbols · ST-745 _dcPuzzleSeed + SHA256 chain · ST-746 DET-CHAIN default root · ST-747 _bitmaskScan is function · ST-748 BITWISE-MASK sub-mode branches · ST-749 _xorMutScan is function · ST-750 XOR-MUT mutation + HW cap · ST-751 3 hidden options in #strategy · ST-752 3 _STRAT_META entries · ST-753 _STRAT_MODE_MAP all includes all 3 · ST-754 _STRAT_MODE_MAP xpoint6 includes all 3 · ST-755 single mode excluded · ST-756 panels injected in DOM · ST-757 stopHunt() cascade · ST-758 startHunt() delegation blocks.     🦞 Audit Response Pack (Phase 87 · v3.4.28 no-bump) — Three surgical patches landed in response to the chat audit. ST-821 — window.safeBigInt(val): new crash-safe BigInt coercion utility placed immediately after _b2hSafe in the BigInt-utility cluster. Three-branch logic — bigint passthrough → 0x-prefixed string → bare numeric/decimal/hex — wrapped in try/catch with 0n fallback so boundary comparisons (zone in/out, advisory range, KITT/LK/All-Puzzles intel surfaces) never throw a TypeError on a mis-typed source. ST-822 — _addKittIntelOverlay rAF decoupling: scanner:tick no longer paints synchronously. New _rAFPending + _latestKittHex closure pair captures the latest hex per tick and drains it on the next requestAnimationFrame (with a setTimeout(16) fallback). _THROTTLE_MS dropped 500 → 300 ms — rAF is now the cadence gate, fewer dropped frames during heavy multi-puzzle scans, no behavioural regression. ST-823 — CWVG BroadcastChannel relay + #cwvgGateModePill (closes Roadmap Item #2 below): when SharedArrayBuffer is unavailable (most file:// sessions, missing COOP/COEP), worker FOUND signals previously had no cross-worker relay path. A same-origin BroadcastChannel('bphks-cwvg-v1') now mirrors the verdict; host cwvgSignalFound is wrapped to also broadcast, and inbound BC {t:'found',wi} messages mirror back into the SAB path via _nclLayer.cwvgSignalFound. New 🚦 CWVG pill inside #kittIntelOverlay surfaces the active transport: SAB (green) when verdict buffer is shared, BC (amber) when BroadcastChannel is the relay, HOST (muted) when neither is available — closes the silent-fail UX gap. Diagnostics: window._nclLayer.cwvgGateMode(), cwvgBC, cwvgRelayFound, cwvgPillRefresh. ST-821/822/823 added; self-test ceiling: ≈728+/ST-828 (incl. ST-824→ST-828 Hardening Pack).     🦞Phase 88 — Audit Response Pack II: BUG-RA-INSIGHT-DETACHED-TR FIX · ST-829v3.5.0 · build 2026.11.08 · no version bump
    🦞 BUG-RA-INSIGHT-DETACHED-TR FIX (Phase 88 · v3.4.28 no-bump) — Reported via a pasted device console log showing hundreds of identical stack traces in a tight burst during an active multi-puzzle scan. BUG-RA-INSIGHT-DETACHED-TR (HIGH): _injectInsightRow(tr, hex) is invoked from two deferred requestIdleCallback sites — the KB Insight batch inside _kbRender and the Recent Attempts path inside _augmentRaRow — both queued with a {timeout: 300} fallback, so the callback can fire up to 300ms after the tr reference was captured. Under load, pushRecent() trims #recentBody to MAX_RECENT via removeChild(recentBody.lastChild), and _kbRender() rebuilds #kbBody wholesale on re-render/page-navigation — both detach the original <tr> from the document before the queued idle callback runs. The function's trailing tr.parentNode.insertBefore(insightTr, tr.nextSibling) then threw TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'insertBefore') against the stale row, repeating on every fired callback. Fix: _injectInsightRow now returns immediately — if (!tr || !tr.parentNode) return; — before any insight-scoring computation, plus a defense-in-depth re-check immediately before the trailing insertBefore() call. Zero behavioural change when the row is still attached (the common case); skips the entire scoring pipeline on the failure path instead of running it and then discarding the result. 🐛 SWEEP-88: also repaired a pre-existing markup bug in this very Development History panel — the Phase 87 card above was missing its closing </details> tag, which silently nested this Roadmap section inside the Phase 87 collapsible instead of as an independent sibling card. ST-829 added (source-pattern assertion against _injectInsightRow.toString(), wired into the Phase 87 Hardening Pack runner). Self-test ceiling: ≈729+/ST-829. VersionGuard green (no bump). Zero changes to scan correctness, cryptographic workers, or insight-scoring math. — 🦞 claude.ai research · 🔬 zync · 🐉 dra69on · 👾 aoxy · 🦋 agnarez · ❤️‍🔥 0xindy · 🐇 0xfinu
    🗺️Next Phases — Roadmap Notes (signalled gaps & feature debt audit)as of v3.4.26 · build 2026.06.13 · 🦞 claude.ai research
    🗺️ Roadmap audit (Phase 80+ candidates) — No phase work has shipped against these items; they are not yet implemented. Each was identified from an architectural stub, an intentional scope-exclusion guard, or a one-way data flow already present in the v3.4.25 codebase. Listed for planning only — no functional, version, or self-test changes accompany this entry.

    1. Dev-History documentation backfill (Phases 43–73, 77–79) — The Changelog (changelogVersionAnchor) and the Feature Spec self-test ceiling line document Phases 43 through 79 in detail (e.g. ST-672 Phase 52, ST-699–705 Phase 62/63, ST-759–761 Phase 77, ST-762 Phase 78, ST-763–766 Phase 79 NCL), but this Development History panel jumps from Phase 42 straight to Phases 74–76 — Phases 43–73, 77, and 78, and the Phase 79 NCL card itself, have no dh-ph-N entry here. Candidate: a documentation-only sync pass that backfills the missing cards from the existing Changelog prose (zero functional risk, VersionGuard no-bump).

    2. §NCL-1 CWVG non-SharedArrayBuffer fallback — The Phase 79 Chained Worker Verdict Gate is explicitly a graceful no-op when SAB unavailable (file://) — which is the default condition for this single-file app opened directly from disk on most mobile browsers. Today, opening via file:// silently disables cross-worker FOUND-signalling with no UI indication. Candidate: a BroadcastChannel / postMessage-relay fallback gate for non-SAB contexts, plus a status pill so the user knows which gate mode (SAB vs. relay vs. none) is active.

    3. DET-CHAIN ⛓ / BITWISE-MASK ⊞ / XOR-MUT ⊕ — single-puzzle mode — Phase 76 intentionally excludes these three strategies from single-puzzle mode via the _STRAT_MODE_MAP guard + a guard toast. The underlying derivations (_dcPuzzleSeed, AND/XOR/LSHIFT sub-modes, HW-capped XOR mutation) are puzzle-scoped and not inherently multi-puzzle. Candidate: extend _STRAT_MODE_MAP's single set to include all 3, scoped to allPuz[singlePuzzleIdx], with matching _STRAT_META status hints and 3 new self-tests mirroring ST-743–758.

    4. MLP §N — full forward-pass replacing the W4 proxy — The Phase 60+61 KB Intelligence MLP block reads _mlpEngine.getW4(bits) as a per-puzzle W4 proxy (FIX-MLP-W4-BITS), not a full network forward pass. Candidate: wire the remaining W1–W3 layers into a real forward-pass producing a pattern-score contribution, feeding the Signal Verdict Engine's existing "MLP W4 ×N pts" slot with a true inference value instead of a single-weight proxy.

    5. CPAE → PIL promotion path — Phase 65's _cpaePilAdvisory is explicitly advisory-only and never writes _pilZoneOverride (by design, to avoid silently overriding PIL's own corpus-derived zones). Candidate: an opt-in "🔗 Promote to PIL zone" action on the violet CPAE advisory badge in _injectInsightRow, gated behind a confirmation toast, that copies {lo,hi} into _pilZoneOverride[bits] with a provenance flag (source:'cpae') so it can be distinguished/reverted later.

    6. §ON-1 Online Corpus Sync → §CM-2 Mutation Engine auto-merge — §ON-1 (opt-in, fetch-only, zero-outbound) currently surfaces a sync status line but solved-puzzle entries it retrieves are not automatically validated/committed into the live corpus — that path still requires the manual §CM-4 Community JSON Import flow. Candidate: an opt-in "auto-commit validated entries" toggle on the Online Sync panel that runs each fetched entry through the existing §CM-2 key→address validation before calling the same commit path as corpusMutCommit.

    7. PIL Bimodality / Proximity signals → ACA & APD zone builders — Phase 74's _detectBimodality() and _pilProximityWeight() currently feed only the PIL DNA/FP zone objects and the SVE pilBimodal/pilProxW score terms. The ACA NOVA band model and the four _apdBuild*Zone() builders (relPos/delta/markov/entropy) do not yet consume either signal. Candidate: expose _detectBimodality()/_pilProximityWeight() as shared cross-engine helpers (already global-readable) and add small SVE-scored bonuses to ACA §O and APD §K analogous to INT-2's pilBimodal/pilProxW terms.

    8. Signal Verdict Engine — restore a fifth tier — Phases 66–69 corrected the SVE palette from a 5-tier (STRONG/MODERATE-HIGH/MODERATE/LOW/BLIND) to the 4-tier (STRONG #22c55e / MODERATE-HIGH #f59e0b / MODERATE #f97316 / BLIND #374151) palette confirmed against HTML ground truth. The resulting MODERATE band (≈15–50% of MAX_PTS, now 68 after Phase 79's NSD bonus) spans a wide score range with a single colour/label. Candidate: re-introduce a MODERATE-LOW tier between MODERATE and BLIND once a ground-truth threshold is agreed, giving _sveStartHook's tiered-override logic a finer soft-override band.

    9. Genetic Sweep — corpus feedback loop — 🧬 Founder injection currently flows one-way (KB → Bridge → GA population seed). The GA's fittest individuals each generation are never written back into the live corpus (§CM-1/§CM-2) or surfaced to PIL/APD as candidate zone centres. Candidate: a "📤 Promote top individual" action in the [View gene pool] modal that runs the GA's best candidate through the same §CM-2 validation path as a corpus-mutation entry (rejected if it doesn't validate — GA candidates are not assumed to be solved keys).

    10. SyncBus topic registry — The 3FSN SyncBus has accumulated many ad-hoc topics across phases (apd:zone-set, aca:zone-set, cpae:advisory, scanner:tick, scanner:started/stopped/recent/stats, etc.) with no single discoverability surface — each new engine author greps prior phases to find the right topic name. Candidate: a small SyncBus.topics static map (topic → {emitters[], listeners[], payload shape}) populated incrementally, plus a debug-only "📡 SyncBus Monitor" panel (behind the existing Verbose toggle) that live-logs topic/payload pairs.

    Prioritisation note: items 1 (docs), 6, and 10 are zero/low functional risk (documentation + opt-in toggles). Items 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 9 touch scan-strategy routing or scoring and should each ship with their own dedicated self-test block (ST-767+) following the established pattern, with VersionGuard bumps where SELF_FILENAME / self-test ceiling counts change. — 🦞 claude.ai research · 🔬 zync · 🐉 dra69on · 👾 aoxy · 🦋 agnarez · ❤️‍🔥 0xindy · 🐇 0xfinu

    🗺️ Numbered roadmap candidates (Phase 80–84) — Concrete phase-number proposals for the gaps catalogued above. Not yet implemented — no functional, version, or self-test changes accompany this entry.

    Phase 80 — NCL v1.1.0: Worker-Side NCL Bridge ⚡ — §NCL-2 BPR is currently host-side only: the sorted Uint32 prefix table rejects candidates after a worker posts a batch back to the host. Pushing the BPR table + NSD tier weights into the worker blob would let rejection happen inside each hash160() loop before any postMessage — and feeding §NCL-3 NSD scores back into the worker's own batch-weighting closes the loop the host-only design left open. Scope: all78 + xpoint6 only (mirrors the existing §NCL scope-gate via _nclScopeAllowed()). Estimated ~4 new self-tests (ST-767→ST-770).

    Phase 81 — corrected: no Phase-72 gap exists — A prior pass of this roadmap flagged Phase 72 as missing from the changelog. That flag is incorrect: Phase 72 — "RN Keyword Search + Phase Jump Index" — is present, shipping the #rnSearchInput release-notes search box + #dhJumpIndex jump-index grid (ST-728/ST-729/ST-730). No gap-fill audit is needed for Phase 72. This slot is left open for the next genuinely-identified documentation gap (see item 1 in the roadmap card above, which remains the real backfill target — Phases 43–73 minus 72, plus 77–78).

    Phase 82 — SWEEP-82: Dead Code Audit 🧹 — SWEEP-73 (Phase 73) removed the THEMES alias, the _DEAD_ZONE_THRESH var, and phantom #enableDeadZoneSkip/#deadZoneThresh DOM. Six phases later (79) introduced the NCL module with its own "pre-integration" fixup comment (FIX-NCL-2: pilFp top-bucket label typo corrected pre-integration) plus several Phase 66–69 zombie surfaces are candidates: any leftover kbApdV220Panel self-test-only stub markers, and APD §K comments referencing pre-_apdTypeSpec per-strategy code paths superseded by the Phase 60+61 unified loop. Candidate scope for a follow-up sweep: grep for pre-integration, TODO, legacy, and orphaned data-stub elements; confirm each is either load-bearing (self-test scaffolding) or removable.

    Phase 83 — APD-Learn v2.3.0 + ACA Oracle v2.1.0 🌌⚡ — The BPMH → BPHKS port pipeline (Phases 74/75 ported PIL v2.2→v2.3 Bimodality/Proximity and PDR/CSR diversity) is open-ended; APD-Learn remains at v2.2.0 and ACA Oracle at v2.0.0 per the footer credits, both unchanged since before Phase 74. Candidate: audit the upstream BPMH branch for APD/ACA improvements analogous to Phase 74's PIL upgrade, and extend the Signal Verdict Engine's MAX_PTS (68 after Phase 79's §NCL-3 NSD bonus) with new APD v2.3/ACA v2.1 score terms — following the same INT-1/INT-2/INT-3/INT-4 pattern Phase 74 used for PIL.

    Phase 84 — NCL v2.0.0: §NCL-5 Adaptive Batch Gating ⚡ — Natural extension of the Phase 79 NCL suite: a fifth module (ABG) that reads the §NCL-3 NSD discretization tier (PRIME/STRONG/.../NULL) per worker and dynamically resizes that worker's batch size — PRIME-tier signals shrink the batch for a focused sweep near a high-confidence zone, NULL/WEAK tiers grow it for broader random coverage. Like §NCL-1–4, gated on _nclScopeAllowed() (all78/xpoint6 only) with zero cost in single-puzzle mode.

    🎯 Scan Strategies
    𔓎 Auto · Smart Picker
    Auto-selects the best strategy for the current mode and puzzle size: xpoint6 → Seg-Rand; multi-puzzle → Seg-Rand; single ≤64b → Epoch; single 65b+ → Seg-Rand. All 78 active puzzles are 71–160b, so Auto always resolves to Seg-Rand.
    ☘︎ ݁Random
    Fully random key picks across the entire selected puzzle's keyspace. Maximum entropy per key.
    ♞ Seg-Rand · 1M Blocks
    Randomly picks a puzzle and a random start offset, then scans sequentially for a configurable block (10K–100M keys). Combines random puzzle selection with cache-friendly sequential access.
    ➤ Sequential
    Monotonically increments from the range minimum to the maximum. Deterministic, full-coverage, low-overhead.
    ⏭ Stride
    Jumps by a configurable stride value rather than incrementing by 1. Useful for distributing scan coverage across a puzzle's range at a fixed interval.
    𖠘 Walk
    Computes a WASM incremental point-add (addG) on each step instead of a full scalar multiply. Extremely fast for dense sequential scanning — uses pre-allocated buffers.
    ♻ Epoch Cursor
    Each puzzle gets one monotonic cursor starting at a random position. Every block advances the cursor by blockSize. Guarantees full puzzle coverage before any position is re-scanned. Wraps emit an EPOCH_WRAP message to the Activity Log.
    ☢ LCG Sweep · No-Repeat
    Builds a virtual block-address space spanning all selected puzzles combined. Uses a random coprime stride (BigInt GCD + rejection sampling) so the full period visits every block exactly once per epoch in a pseudo-random order. Handles up to 2160-range puzzles without overflow.
    𓃰 BSGS · Baby-Step Giant-Step
    O(√N) algebraic search targeted at puzzles #50–#70. Pre-computes a configurable baby-step table (16–24 bits, ≈256 KB–≈2 GB JS Map RAM), then strides through giant-steps. Most effective on mid-range single puzzles.
    🦘 Kangaroo · Pollard's Rho
    O(√N) Pollard's Rho kangaroo algorithm for puzzles with a known public key. Maintains tame and wild kangaroo walkers that collide on the target discrete logarithm. Best used for single xpoint6 puzzles.
    ♠ Gaussian · Weak-Key Proximity
    Biases key sampling toward user-defined centre points using a Gaussian distribution with configurable σ (0.1–50% of puzzle range). Useful for exploring regions near known weak-key patterns or partial information.
    🧠 APD-Learn v2.2.0 — Adaptive Intelligence Strategies
    Pattern-learning strategies derived from a Bayesian prior over the solved-puzzle corpus. All are educational — statistical patterns from solved keys provide weak priors, not shortcuts.     🧠 APD-Learn
    Biased zone sampler — picks keys weighted by relPos centroid, Hamming weight, and per-position nibble frequency from the solved corpus. Baseline learn strategy.
    🦘🧠 Kangaroo+Learn
    Biased Kangaroo/BSGS — seeds the kangaroo herd from the learned relPos centroid rather than the range midpoint. For xpoint5 known-pubkey puzzles.
    🔗 Markov Nibble Chain
    Samples keys via a bigram/trigram Markov transition matrix built from solved-corpus nibble sequences. Blend weight slider (0=pure RNG → 1=pure Markov). 16×16 heatmap in APD Insight § E.
    📐 Delta Stride
    Computes arithmetic deltas between consecutive solved keys and fits a linear regression. Projects a predicted key window for the target puzzle. ±2σ band visualized in APD Insight § F.
    🔒 Prefix-Lock
    Identifies low-entropy nibble positions (H<2.5 bits) across the corpus and locks them to their most-likely values during sampling. Lock table editor + auto-fill. Min 40% positions remain free.
    🧮 Modular Sieve
    Passive filter layer over any primary strategy — rejects candidates whose residue mod {2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19} diverges from the corpus distribution. χ² significance gate. Strength slider.
    ☯ Entropy Drift
    Entropy-guided random walk — samples each nibble position from a PMF shaped by the per-position Shannon entropy profile of solved keys. Bias slider. Per-position entropy map in APD Insight § H.
    🧬 Genetic Sweep
    Population-based GA on composite pattern fitness (relPos · HW · nibble · Markov). Configurable pop size (16–128), mutation rate μ, crossover. Gene pool snapshot view. Founder injection via KB → Bridge.
    🌡️ Simulated Annealing
    Temperature-controlled walk on the pattern-score landscape. Boltzmann acceptance function — accepts downhill moves with probability e^(−Δ/T). T0, cooling rate, and k% sliders. Re-heat button. Trajectory in APD Insight § I.
    🔄 Auto-Learn
    ε-greedy multi-armed bandit scheduler across all 9 strategies. Evaluates zone hit rate every N epochs and dynamically increases the allocation of the best-performing strategy. Pie chart in APD Insight § J.
    ⚡ §P4 Dead-Zone Skip — Always-Active Acceleration
    Skips batches where all three engines (APD + ACA + PIL) score below a self-calibrating threshold — eliminating wasted compute on statistically dead zones. Always active, no manual toggle required. Self-tests ST-472–ST-474 · ST-485–ST-490.
    ⚡ Tri-Zero Skip
    _deadZoneCheck(lo,hi,bits) evaluates APD + ACA + PIL zone scores before every batch dispatch. If all three engines score below threshold, the batch is skipped and the zone is advanced immediately.
    🎯 Sliding-Window Auto-Adjust
    _dzAutoAdjust() recalibrates _DZ_AUTO_THRESH every 200 checks toward a 25% target skip rate. Threshold raised if skip rate <12.5%, lowered if >37.5%. Bounds: 1e-9 … 0.5. No manual slider needed.
    📊 Live Rate Display
    Auto-skip rate and current threshold shown live in the Safety & Audit panel as #dzAutoSkipRate. Updates every recalibration window.

    §S Signed Status v1.0 & N·0·P Engine v1.0.0

    System burden = DARK×72 + EXPOSED×6 − SOLVED×82 = −10 at current corpus. Surfaces via #nopBurdenSection and #nopBurdenScore DOM elements. mapPuzzleNOP routes per-puzzle status to −1/0/+1 paths.
    🏹 Hunt Modes
    Single Puzzle
    Targets one specific puzzle selected from the dropdown. Full worker parallelism dedicated to a single keyspace range.
    Hunt ALL 78 Puzzles
    Derives hash160 for each key and checks membership against all 77 unsolved puzzle targets simultaneously using a pre-built Set. Combined prize: 903.0 BTC.
    🎯 xpoint6 Mode
    Targets 5 puzzles with published public keys (#140–#160). Matches only the 32-byte x-coordinate of the secp256k1 public key — skips SHA-256 + RIPEMD-160 entirely for ~15–25% extra speed. Combined prize: 75.0 BTC.
    ⚡ Strategy Picker & Per-Strategy Statistics
    • Custom Strategy Picker Modal — A styled button replaces the native OS <select> picker. Tapping opens a bottom-sheet modal listing all 28 strategies with emoji, name, description, and live per-strategy statistics. The hidden <select> is kept fully intact for code and self-test compatibility.
    • Per-Strategy Statistics — Three counters tracked per strategy, persisted to localStorage key bph_stratperf_v1 across sessions: 🗝 Keys (total keys scanned while active), ⏱ Time (wall-clock seconds from start→stop), 🔄 Epochs (EPOCH_WRAP events received — epoch/lcgsweep only).
    • Strategy Performance Monitor Card — A persistent live card on the main scan panel shows all strategies with key counts, time, epoch counts, and live k/s average. Auto-refreshes every 1.5 s during scanning.
    • ● Active Indicator — The currently-scanning strategy shows a live "● ACTIVE" badge in both the picker modal and the monitor card.
    • Keyboard & Accessibility — Picker rows are tabindex="0", role="radio", respond to Enter / Space; Escape closes the sheet; backdrop click closes.
    🔬 Match & Verification Modes
    hash160 Match
    Derives SHA-256 → RIPEMD-160 → 20-byte hash160 for each public key. Checks against the puzzle's expected hash160. The standard Bitcoin P2PKH match method.
    Address Match
    Computes the full Base58Check P2PKH address (1…) and compares it to the puzzle's known address. Useful for confirming a candidate key against a human-readable address.
    xpoint Match
    Extracts only the 32-byte x-coordinate of the public key point and compares against the known pubkey's x-coordinate. Fastest mode — bypasses hash functions entirely.
    Uint32 Hash160 Prefilter
    In hash160 mode, the first 4 bytes of each candidate hash are packed as a big-endian Uint32 and tested against a prefix-Set before the full 40-char hex comparison. Rejects non-matches ~3–4× faster.
    ⚙️ Engine & WASM Architecture
    • WASM secp256k1 — Jacobian point-add / point-double / addMixed / batch modular inversion (Montgomery ladder). Affine _pw precomputes loaded once at boot.
    • WASM RIPEMD-160 — WebAssembly implementation of the full RIPEMD-160 digest. Used for hash160 derivation.
    • WASM SHA-256 — ~5× faster than JS for 33-byte compressed pubkeys. SHA-256 K-constants pre-built as a Uint8Array and memcpy'd once at init (eliminates 64× setUint32 calls).
    • SHA256→RIPEMD160 Fused Path — Single WASM call computes both digests in one pass (Perf-8). Eliminates the JS-side intermediate buffer copy between SHA-256 output and RIPEMD-160 input.
    • Blob-URL Web Workers — All engine code runs in dedicated Web Workers spawned from Blob URLs. Network egress only to the allowlisted Live Sync hosts (mempool.space, blockstream.info, raw.githubusercontent.com). CSP enforced: connect-src 'self' blob: data: https://api.coingecko.com https://raw.githubusercontent.com https://mempool.space https://blockstream.info (v3.5.0: mempool.space + blockstream.info added for Live Sync verification).
    • Worker Watchdog — Each worker emits a heartbeat every 3 s. Main thread detects stalls after ~9 s and auto-respawns dead workers. Respawn count surfaced in stat boxes.
    • WASM Pre-warm — A disposable warm-up worker spawns 2 s after page load to compile and cache WebAssembly modules. Subsequent workers skip compilation and call WebAssembly.instantiate(module) directly (Perf-6).
    • SIMD Detection & Adaptive Batch — Runtime WebAssembly.validate() probe detects SIMD support and adapts batch sizing accordingly (Perf-7).
    • HEX Lookup Table (LUT) — 256-entry _HEX_LUT replaces all .toString(16).padStart(2,'0') calls in the hot path. +15–25% k/s.
    • 64 KB RNG Buffer — Enlarged from 4 KB; 16× fewer crypto.getRandomValues() refills. +1–3% k/s.
    • Pre-allocated Batch Buffers — _pubsBuf / _shasBuf reused across batches, eliminating per-iteration GC pressure. +2–4% k/s.
    • xpoint Uint8Array Byte Pool — Zero-string-allocation x-coordinate comparison path for xpoint6 mode (Perf-10). +3–8% k/s in xpoint6 mode.
    🔑 Key Browser
    • Browse private key ranges across all 77 unsolved puzzles in a paginated table (32–1024 keys/page). All arithmetic uses BigInt — 100% offline, no network.
    • Follow Scan — Live toggle auto-navigates to the page containing each new key as the scanner runs.
    • Jump to Key — Enter any hex key or decimal value to jump directly to its page.
    • → KB buttons in Recent Attempts and History tabs jump instantly to the Key Browser page containing that key.
    • On FOUND event: Key Browser auto-switches to the discovered key's page with a 400 ms deferred tab click.
    • Page ID mirrors the privatekeyfinder.io page format — decimal value of the first key on the page.
    • 🧠 KB Intelligence (v2.2.0) — Smart panel above the table with 4 tools:
      • 🔬 Insight Mode — Toggle expands every KB row with a live 32-nibble frequency heatmap (green = above-corpus-mean, red = below) plus a full pattern-score breakdown (relPos · HW · relScore% · hwScore% · nibScore%) and "How unusual?" verdict (🟢🟡🟠🔴).
      • ⭐ Strategy Recommender — Modal showing per-strategy ★ ratings (1–5) derived from corpus statistics: σ confidence for learn, χ² for Markov, Δ variance for delta-stride, lock count for prefix-lock, significance count for sieve.
      • 📈 Pattern Timeline — SVG chart of all 160 puzzles: green dots for solved keys' relPos, amber ±1σ / red ±2σ bands for unsolved predictions. Centroid trend line overlaid.
      • 📊 Scan History Overlay — Per-strategy keys scanned, wall-time, throughput, and epoch count since last session start.
    • [→ Bridge] per-row button — Every KB row has a Bridge button that opens a 4-option seed modal:
      • 🌡️ Annealing seed — Sets the key as the Simulated Annealing walk start; re-heats to T0 and switches strategy.
      • 📐 Delta stride origin — Sets the key as the arithmetic origin for the delta-stride projection.
      • 🧬 Genetic founder — Injects the key into the genetic population as a founder individual (deduplicated).
      • 🔒 Prefix-lock template — Extracts corpus-high-frequency nibble positions from the key and pre-fills the lock table; switches to prefix-lock strategy.
    🔍 Key Inspector
    Enter any private key (hex) to instantly derive its public key, hash160, and Bitcoin address entirely offline. Checks the result against all 78 puzzle targets. Results deduplicated across repeated calls. Fully offline, BigInt fallback when WASM is unavailable.
    🔔 Match Alert System
    • Web Audio Chimes — 3-note ascending chime via the Web Audio API on each match. Unique base frequency per xpoint6 puzzle (A-minor pentatonic scale: 440–1175 Hz). Works in background tabs.
    • Desktop Notifications — Browser Notification API alert showing puzzle number and BTC prize. Permission requested on demand.
    • Full-screen Found Overlay — Dismissible modal with green glow showing puzzle, address, private key (WIF), and a one-click copy button.
    • Preview Buttons — Test each chime tone before scanning.

    🚗 KITT Adaptive Engine Visualizer
    An animated beam-track inspired by KITT from Knight Rider visualizes real cryptographic throughput. The animation speed (--kitt-scan-dur) is set by JS based on live k/s measurements:
    • Idle — Organic lub-dub heartbeat. Slow, soft, dim.
    • Scanning — Crisp ping-pong bounce. Speed proportional to k/s. Batch pulse overlay fires on each 250 ms worker tick.
    • Struggle — Heavy, blurred, sluggish — detects worker stalls and respawn events.

    💾 Persistence, Safety & QoL
    • Scan Resume — On page reload after an unexpected close, an amber prompt offers to restore the last scan configuration (mode, puzzle, workers). Stale markers (>24 h or zero progress) are silently discarded.
    • Session History — Last N scanning sessions stored in localStorage with start/stop times, duration, mode, k/s, matches, and end reason. Exportable as JSON.
    • Activity Log — In-app event panel capturing scan lifecycle events, WASM init status, watchdog respawns, self-test results, and key discoveries. Max 200 rows, filter by INFO / ENGINE / WARN / ERR / FOUND. Exportable as TXT or JSON.
    • Per-Strategy Stats — Persistent localStorage counters (keys, time, epochs) per strategy, accumulated across sessions and visible live in the Strategy Performance card and picker modal.
    • Auto Background Scan — Scheduled scan start/stop with optional daily or weekly recurrence. Wake-lock acquisition keeps the scan alive during screen sleep.
    • Tuning Presets — Balanced / Mobile-friendly / Desktop / Turbo — applies tested (workers, batch, delayMs) combos to live workers instantly.
    • Remember Settings — Last session settings auto-restored on next page load.
    • PWA Manifest — Enables "Add to Home Screen" install prompt on mobile browsers. Full standalone display mode.
    • AbortController Shutdown — Prevents zombie workers on stop+restart race conditions. Watchdog interval cleared atomically with worker termination.
    • XSS Hardening — All dynamic content rendered via innerHTML passes through escH() HTML-escape helper.
    • Haptic Feedback — Micro-vibration on tab switch, scan start/stop, copy, and key found events (where supported).

    🔒 Security & Privacy
    • 100% Offline — Zero external network egress confirmed. No Cloudflare beacon, analytics pixel, font CDN, or any external fetch.
    • Strict CSP — default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' blob: data: https://api.coingecko.com https://raw.githubusercontent.com https://mempool.space https://blockstream.info; worker-src 'self' blob:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'.
    • CSPRNG — All random key generation uses crypto.getRandomValues() exclusively. Math.random() not used in any cryptographic context.
    • Blob Worker URLs — Worker source compiled into a Blob URL at runtime. Revoked after use to release memory.
    • Single File — Entire application ships as one self-contained HTML file. No build step, no external dependencies at runtime.

    🧬
    WASM · Workers · BigInt
    BPH KITT Scanner is a single-file, 100% offline Bitcoin Puzzle scanner. It derives secp256k1 public keys and Bitcoin addresses from private key candidates (random, sequential, or algorithmic) and checks them against the 78 currently-unsolved Bitcoin Puzzles. All cryptography runs in WebAssembly workers — secp256k1 point multiplication, SHA-256, RIPEMD-160, and batch modular inversion. No server, no network calls, no external dependencies, no tracking beacons.
    ⚠️ Educational Tool — Cryptographic Lottery. The probability of solving an unsolved Bitcoin Puzzle by random scanning is astronomically low. Cryptographically lucky outcomes are theoretically possible but effectively impossible in practice. This is a research, educational, and engineering tool.
    ⚡ Quick Start Up and scanning in under 60 seconds
    1
    Open the HTML file in your browser.
    Drag BPHKS_V3_4_12_CLD.html into Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari. No server needed — all crypto loads from embedded WASM bytes. Wait for "✅ All N assertions green" in the Activity Log before scanning.
    2
    Select a Hunt Mode.
    Use the Mode dropdown. For your first run, choose Hunt ALL 78 puzzles simultaneously — this casts the widest net across all unsolved puzzles, ranging from 71-bit to 160-bit key ranges.
    3
    Choose a Strategy.
    Leave Strategy on Auto for your first run. For All-77 it resolves to Seg-Rand with dynamic inverse-coverage bias — the most effective multi-puzzle coverage algorithm.
    4
    Apply a Tuning Preset.
    Open the Preset dropdown. Choose Balanced for desktop, Mobile-friendly for phones, or ⚡ Turbo for maximum throughput.
    5
    Press ▶ Start.
    The KITT scanner bar animates, workers initialize WASM modules, and keys-per-second climbs to cruise speed within ~5 seconds. Watch the Activity Log for engine boot messages and any matches.
    💡 Tip: Enable Match Alerts. Check 🔔 Alert and ensure your browser allows notifications. On a match the app plays a chime, flashes the tab title, sends a desktop notification, and triggers haptic feedback on mobile.
    🎯 Hunt Mode: Single Puzzle value="single" · Focus on one puzzle at a time
    Single mode focuses all workers on exactly one selected puzzle. Use the puzzle selector to pick from any of the 77 unsolved puzzles. You can set a Custom Range (Range Min / Range Max) to restrict scanning to a hex sub-range within the puzzle's published bounds. Strategies that require a single puzzle — Sequential, Stride, Walk, BSGS, and Kangaroo — are only effective in Single mode.
    1.After choosing Single mode, select your target puzzle by puzzle number (bits). Puzzles are 71–160 bits.
    2.Optionally enter hex values in Range Min and Range Max. These are clamped to the puzzle's published bounds. Leave blank to scan the full range.
    3.For small puzzles (≤64 bits): Epoch Cursor guarantees full coverage. For larger puzzles: Seg-Rand or LCG Sweep. For known-pubkey puzzles (#135+): consider BSGS or Kangaroo.
    📌 Auto-Slice across Workers: When enabled in Advanced Settings, Sequential and Walk strategies automatically partition the range into N equal sub-ranges — one per worker — eliminating duplicate work.
    ☯ Hunt Mode: All 78 Puzzles value="all" · Default recommended mode
    All-77 mode loads all 78 currently-unsolved Bitcoin Puzzle ranges into every worker. Each generated key is checked against all 78 targets in the same batch pass — at virtually no extra CPU cost (the Bloom filter prefilter rejects >99.998% of non-matching candidates before the full hash160 check). Dynamic puzzle weighting biases selection toward puzzles that have been scanned less.
    1.Select "Hunt ALL 78 puzzles simultaneously". No puzzle picker appears — all 78 ranges are loaded automatically.
    2.Set Match Mode to hash160 (fastest). Skips full Base58Check address derivation. ~15–25% faster than address mode.
    3.Strategy: Auto or Seg-Rand. Auto resolves to Seg-Rand for multi-puzzle mode — scans random 1M-key blocks with dynamic bias toward less-scanned puzzles.
    4.Enable Dynamic Puzzle Weight in Advanced Settings. This biases scanning toward under-scanned puzzles for coverage fairness.
    🔑 Hunt Mode: xpoint6 5 known-pubkey puzzles · 75.0 BTC combined
    xpoint6 targets the 5 Bitcoin Puzzles that have known public keys (#140 · #145 · #150 · #155 · #160). Matching is done by comparing the x-coordinate of the derived public key against the known target — skipping SHA-256 and RIPEMD-160 entirely. This makes xpoint6 ~15–25% faster than hash160 mode while targeting 75.0 BTC combined. Workers only receive the 5 known-pubkey ranges, making this ~13× more efficient than All-77 + xpoint match mode.
    1.Select "Hunt 5 known-pubkey puzzles (xpoint6)". Match Mode auto-locks to xpoint.
    2.Strategy: Auto (resolves to Seg-Rand). Note: Kangaroo only targets puzzle #140 — use it in Single mode for a focused attack.
    3.xpoint6 uses bit-count proportional weighting: #140→18.7%, #145→19.3%, #150→20.0%, #155→20.7%, #160→21.3%.
    🔬 Known Public Keys: Puzzles #140–#160 had their public keys revealed on the Bitcoin blockchain via an older uncompressed transaction. This allows x-coordinate matching instead of full hash160 derivation.
    🔍 Match Modes How candidate keys are checked against puzzle targets
    ⚡ hash160 · Fastest RECOMMENDED
    RIPEMD-160(SHA-256(pubkey)) — 20-byte hash. Bloom filter prefilter + Uint32 prefix check. No Base58Check needed. Best for All-77 and Single.
    🏛 address · Base58Check
    Full P2PKH address (1xxx…) via hash160 + version byte + double-SHA256 checksum + Base58. ~10–15% slower. Use for visual verification.
    🎯 xpoint · Public Key X
    Matches the 32-byte x-coordinate directly. Skips SHA-256 and RIPEMD-160. Fastest mode. Only useful for puzzles #140, #145, #150, #155, #160. Auto-locked for xpoint6.
    Mode Derivation Path Speed Best For
    hash160privkey → pubkey → SHA256 → RIPEMD160⚡⚡⚡ FastestAll-77, Single
    addresshash160 → +version → double-SHA256 → Base58⚡⚡ FastSingle, verbose runs
    xpointprivkey → pubkey → x-coordinate only⚡⚡⚡⚡ Fastestxpoint6 mode only
    Strategies
    🤖 Auto · Smart Strategy Picker value="auto" · Resolves at scan-start
    Auto consults the current Hunt Mode, puzzle count, and bit-size at the moment Start is pressed, then resolves to the optimal concrete strategy. The resolved strategy is logged in the Activity Log.
    if mode === 'xpoint6' → Seg-Rand
    else if puzzles > 1 (all-78) → Seg-Rand
    else if puzzle.bits ≤ 64 → Epoch Cursor
    else (single, bits 65–160) → Seg-Rand
    ☘ Random · Pure CSPRNG value="random"
    Each key in every batch is drawn independently and uniformly at random using a 64 KB CSPRNG buffer (refreshed via crypto.getRandomValues()). No positional correlation between keys. Limitation: Seg-Rand is strictly superior for all use cases — use Random only when you need pure statistical independence.
    ♞ Seg-Rand · 1M Blocks value="segrand"
    Randomly picks a puzzle and a random start position, then scans sequentially for a configurable block (10K–100M keys, default 1M). Combines random puzzle selection with cache-friendly sequential access. Auto strategy for single puzzles >64 bits.
    Block Size~BatchesBest For
    10 K≈ 10High puzzle diversity, small puzzles
    1 M (default)≈ 977All hardware, recommended
    100 M≈ 97,657Near-sequential for very large puzzles
    ♻ Epoch Cursor · Full Sweep value="epoch"
    Each active puzzle gets one independent monotonic cursor starting at a random position. Every block advances the cursor by blockSize. When the cursor passes the puzzle's upper bound, it wraps — completing one epoch — and an EPOCH_WRAP event is logged. Guarantees full coverage before any position is re-scanned. Enable Coverage Map for session-persistent block tracking.
    ☢ LCG Sweep · No-Repeat value="lcgsweep" · no-repeat epoch scanner
    Builds a virtual block-address space spanning all selected puzzles combined (T = Σ⌈span_i / blockSize⌉). Picks a random starting index v₀ and a random coprime stride r (BigInt GCD + rejection sampling). The LCG sequence visits every block across every puzzle exactly once per epoch in a cryptographically random-looking order. All arithmetic is BigInt — handles up to 2¹⁶⁰-range puzzles without overflow.
    🧬 Mathematical Guarantee: A coprime stride r relative to total T guarantees the sequence {v₀ + k·r mod T} is a permutation of {0,1,…,T-1} — every block visited exactly once per epoch.
    ➤ Sequential · Linear Scan value="seq" · Single puzzle only
    Monotonically scans from pz.lo → pz.hi in order, then wraps (emitting SEQ_WRAP). Single puzzle mode only — overridden to random in multi-puzzle mode. Enable Auto-slice range across workers to partition the range into N non-overlapping sub-ranges. Use Custom Range (Range Min/Max) to restrict to a hex sub-range.
    ⏭ Stride · Fixed-Step Interleaved value="stride" · Single puzzle only
    Scans keys at fixed intervals: start, start+S, start+2S, … where S is the configured stride size (1–16,777,216, default 1024). Useful for distributing scanning across multiple independent browser instances — Instance 0 starts at offset 0 with stride=N, Instance 1 at offset 1, etc. A Stride Span Hint shows the stride as a percentage of the puzzle range.
    〰 Walk · EC-Add Chain value="walk" · Fastest sequential throughput
    Like Sequential but uses a fast EC-add shortcut: first key derived via full scalar multiply, subsequent keys via addG — eliminating repeated expensive scalar multiplications. Public key stays in WASM memory between batches, saving ~66 KB of redundant memory writes per batch. +5–10% k/s over Sequential. Single puzzle mode only. Enable Auto-slice for worker deduplication.
    🔢 BSGS · Baby-Step Giant-Step value="bsgs" · O(√N) · Single puzzle only
    O(√N) meet-in-the-middle algorithm. Builds a baby-step table of 2^T EC points, then takes giant-steps of size 2^T checking for collisions. Configure Baby-Step Table Bits (16–24, default 20). T>24 is refused — a JS Map baby table at T=26 would OOM this VM.
    Table Bits (T)RAMEffective Puzzle Size
    16≈ 256 KBUp to ~32 bits
    20 (default)≈ 100 MB (JS Map)Up to ~40 bits
    24 (max)≈ 1.5–2 GB (JS Map)Up to ~48 bits — T=25/26 refused in v3.5.0
    ⚠️ All active puzzles are 71–160 bits. BSGS is only practical for puzzles significantly below 64 bits — useful as a theoretical/educational tool for the current unsolved set.
    🦘 Kangaroo · Pollard's Rho value="kangaroo" · O(√N) · known-pubkey puzzles
    O(√N) algorithm for the EC discrete logarithm problem when the target public key is known. Runs tame kangaroos (known positions) and wild kangaroos (offset by the unknown DL) — detects a Distinguished Point (DP) collision between them. Configure DP Bits (10–25, default 14). Parallel speedup is linear in worker count. Currently targets puzzle #135 only. Use in Single mode for a focused attack on a specific known-pubkey puzzle.
    🧬 PIL-DNA · DNA Zone Scan value="pil-dna" · Single or All mode · PIL v2.3.0
    Uses the Puzzle Intelligence Layer (PIL) to compute a DNA-optimal scan zone for the selected puzzle. The zone center is derived from the 64-position bit-probability array of solved keys (bit[i]=1 if prob>0.5), mapped into the puzzle's keyspace. Band = ±5% of puzzle span. Internally scans with Seg-Rand within that zone.
    🧬 Click Apply Zone in the PIL Zone row to pre-set Range Min/Max, or start the scan directly — the zone is applied automatically at scan start. Open the 🧬 PIL tab first to initialise the analysis engine.
    🔍 PIL-FP · Fingerprint Zone Scan value="pil-fp" · Single or All mode · PIL v2.3.0
    Uses the Puzzle Intelligence Layer (PIL) fingerprint cluster analysis. For the selected puzzle, builds up to 5 scan zones from RelPos cluster centroids (band = ±2% of span). On first scan start, zone 0 (highest-population cluster) is applied. Use ⏭ Next FP Zone to cycle through the 5 clusters. HW-filter annotation displayed in zone info.
    🔍 Use the §A Auto-Scan in the PIL tab to automatically cycle all FP zones across all puzzles with a configurable dwell timer.
    ⛏️ APD×PIL Fusion · Fused Zone Multi-Hunter value="apd-pil-fusion" · Fusion v1.1.0
    Combines APD and PIL zone predictions into a single tightest-intersection fused zone per puzzle. Up to 8 merged batches cycle across all-78 or xpoint6 multi-hunter. Three dwell modes control batch advancement:
    • Timed — each batch runs for a configurable dwell (30s · 1m · 5m · 15m), then auto-advances.
    • ∞ Infinite — stays on batch 0 forever. Useful for deep single-zone scanning.
    • ⚡ On-Stop — advances batch index the instant a scan halts for any reason (300ms poll). Maximises coverage by eliminating idle time between zones.
    💡 Requires both APD Insight and PIL tabs to have been initialised. Open 🧠 APD Insight and rebuild the corpus, then open 🧬 PIL — both engines load asynchronously. The Fusion panel appears in the main scan strategy row once both are ready. Blinky v1.1.0: amber LED on APD §K tab + cyan LED on PIL §A tab confirm active engine state.
    🌌⛏️ APD+PIL+ACA Triple Fusion · All-Engines Fused Zone Multi-Hunter value="apd-pil-aca-fusion" · Triple Fusion v1.0.0
    Fuses APD Insight × PIL × ACA Oracle zone predictions into a single tightest 3-way intersection per puzzle, with graceful fallback to the best 2-way intersection, then to the tightest single zone — protected by a min-width guard of 2^(bits-10). 8 cycled batches per run combine 4 APD types (insight/delta/markov/entropy) × 2 PIL types (dna/fp) with ACA bands (nova/top1/confweight/combined). Three dwell modes mirror APD×PIL Fusion:
    • Timed — each batch runs for a configurable dwell (30s · 1m · 5m · 15m), then auto-advances.
    • ∞ Infinite — stays on batch 0 forever. Deep single-zone scanning.
    • ⚡ On-Stop — advances batch index the instant a scan halts (300ms poll). Zero idle time between zones.
    💡 Requires APD Insight, PIL, and ACA Oracle to be initialised. Open each tab so all three engines warm up. Fused zones write into window._acaZoneOverride[bits] — the highest-priority slot in the startHunt() zone chain (ACA > APD > PIL > default). Blinky v1.3.0: zone badge shows 🌌⛏️ TRIPLE, and all three engine LEDs (APD amber · PIL cyan · ACA violet) illuminate simultaneously via _tripleFusionEngine.isActive().
    ♠ Gaussian · Weak-Key Proximity value="gaussian"
    Samples private keys from a normal distribution N(center, σ²) via Box-Muller transform around user-configured hex focus points. Keys outside [pz.lo, pz.hi] are clamped via rejection sampling. Configure Gaussian σ (1%/5%/10%/25% of puzzle range) and Centers (64-char hex values, newline/comma separated — defaults to puzzle midpoint).
    σ Setting68% Key RangeUse Case
    1%2% band around centerExtremely specific hypothesis testing
    5% (default)10% band around centerGeneral proximity scanning
    25%50% band around centerNear-uniform with center bias
    🧠 APD-Learn v2.2.0 — Adaptive Intelligence Strategies Pattern-learning from the solved-puzzle corpus
    ⚠️ Educational Notice. Statistical patterns from solved keys provide weak priors — not shortcuts. The actual probability of solving an unsolved Bitcoin Puzzle by any method remains astronomically low. All APD-Learn strategies are governed by the same cryptographic difficulty as random search.
    The APD-Learn engine (window._learnEngine) analyses the solved-puzzle corpus at startup, computing: relPos centroid & σ, Hamming-weight centroid & σ, per-position nibble frequency (16×64 PMF table), per-position Shannon entropy profile, and a linear relPos trend vs. puzzle bits. The APD Insight tab (§ A–J) visualises all computed features live.
    🧠 APD-Learn / Kangaroo+Learn value="learn" · "kangaroo-learn"
    Biased zone sampler weighted by relPos centroid, HW, and nibble frequency. Kangaroo+Learn variant seeds the herd from the learned centroid for xpoint5 known-pubkey puzzles. These are the v2.1.0 foundations — always stable baselines. Configure Learn Weight slider (0=pure RNG → 1=full corpus bias). Toggle composeLockLearn to combine with Prefix-Lock.
    🔗 Markov Nibble Chain value="markov-nibble"
    Samples each nibble position using a bigram (or trigram) transition matrix built from the solved corpus. At each step, with probability markovWeight the next nibble is drawn from the Markov row; otherwise it falls back to pure RNG. Configure: Markov Weight slider, Bigram/Trigram radio toggle. APD Insight § E shows the 16×16 transition heatmap and χ² significance badge.
    💡 Use [→ Use Markov-Nibble Strategy] button in APD Insight § E to switch strategy in one click.
    📐 Delta Stride value="delta-stride"
    Computes normalised deltas between consecutive solved keys (ordered by puzzle bits), fits a linear regression, and projects a predicted relPos window for the target puzzle. Seeds the scanner at lastSolvedKey + predictedDelta ± tolerance (±2σ). APD Insight § F visualises the delta series with ±2σ band. High-variance warning badge shown when σ > 0.20. Use [Apply Delta Window] to set the scan range.
    🔒 Prefix-Lock value="prefix-lock"
    Identifies nibble positions with Shannon entropy H < 2.5 bits and locks them to their most likely values during sampling. At least 40% of positions always remain free. Config: Lock Table Editor (manual per-position nibble list), [Auto-fill from LearnEngine], [Reset to RNG]. Combine with APD-Learn via composeLockLearn checkbox. Alternatively, use the KB → Bridge → 🔒 Prefix-lock button to pre-fill from any browsed key.
    🧮 Modular Sieve value="modular-sieve" · passive filter
    A passive rejection filter over any primary strategy. Builds residue profiles for primes {2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19} from the solved corpus and computes χ² significance per prime. Keys failing the sieve (residue weight below threshold) are discarded before the WASM scalar multiply. Config: Sieve Strength slider (0=off, 1=strict), Enable Sieve checkbox. APD Insight § G shows per-prime residue heatmaps.
    ☯ Entropy Drift value="entropy-drift"
    Generates keys by walking through nibble positions, sampling each from a PMF shaped by the per-position entropy profile of solved keys. Low-entropy positions are sampled from a tighter distribution; high-entropy positions remain near-uniform. Config: Entropy Bias slider. APD Insight § H shows the colour-banded per-position entropy map.
    🧬 Genetic Sweep value="genetic-sweep"
    Maintains a population of candidate keys evaluated by a composite fitness function: relScore·0.35 + hwScore·0.20 + nibScore·0.25 + markovScore·0.20. Each generation: select top-50% by score, apply uniform crossover at configurable bit-flip rate, mutate at rate μ. Config: Population size (16/32/64/128), Mutation rate μ slider, [View gene pool] snapshot. Inject founder individuals via KB → Bridge → 🧬.
    🌡️ Simulated Annealing value="annealing"
    Temperature-controlled walk on the pattern-score landscape. Each step proposes a neighbour (random bit-flip), then accepts with probability e−Δ/T (Boltzmann). Temperature decays each epoch by cooling factor α. Config: T0 (initial temperature), Cooling rate α, Bit-flip k%, [Re-heat] button. APD Insight § I shows the live temperature trajectory. Seed the starting point via KB → Bridge → 🌡️.
    🔄 Auto-Learn · Adaptive Scheduler value="auto-learn"
    ε-greedy multi-armed bandit across all 9 APD strategies. Starts with a corpus-informed prior allocation. Every N epochs it evaluates each strategy's zone hit rate and pattern score, then shifts 90% of allocation to the best-performing strategy and distributes 10% for exploration. Config: [Force rebalance], [Export allocation CSV]. APD Insight § J shows the real-time pie chart and per-strategy performance bars. Recommended for unattended long scans.
    Default allocation: learn 30% · markov-nibble 20% · delta-stride 15% · prefix-lock 15% · modular-sieve 10% · genetic-sweep 5% · annealing 5%
    ⛏️ APD×PIL Fusion v1.1.0 Fused zone multi-hunter · apd-pil-fusion · tightest intersection · 8 batches
    Fusion fuses the APD corpus zone and PIL DNA/FP zone for each puzzle into the tightest valid intersection. Up to 8 merged batches are built per run. Requires both APD Insight and PIL engines to be initialised.
    1
    Initialise both engines first.
    Open 🧠 APD Insight and click Rebuild if the corpus is empty. Then open 🧬 PIL — both load asynchronously. Blinky LEDs will appear on those tabs once active.
    2
    Select apd-pil-fusion from the strategy picker.
    The Fusion panel appears in the strategy row. Choose Hunt Scope (Single · All-77 · xpoint6), select a Dwell Mode, and press ▶ Start.
    3
    Choose a dwell mode.
    Timed advances batches on a countdown. ∞ stays on batch 0 forever. ⚡ On-Stop advances the moment a scan halts — zero idle time between zones, best for maximum coverage cycling.
    💡 Blinky v1.1.0: Amber LED on 🧠 APD Insight tab + cyan LED on 🧬 PIL tab confirm each engine is actively scanning. Panel headers pulse to reinforce which engine owns the current batch.
    🌌 ACA Oracle v2.0.0 — Astronomical Coordination Algorithm 7 sub-panels · 81-corpus KDE · NOVA band · xPoint6 attacks · Tab 4
    ACA Oracle is a standalone analysis suite positioned as the 4th tab (after Key Browser). It derives KDE-based zone predictions from the 81-corpus solved-key distribution and provides tools for per-puzzle deep analysis, corpus visualisation, xPoint6 attack mode planning, and a Recommendations Engine.
    1
    Open the 🌌 ACA Oracle tab.
    It loads automatically — no rebuild needed. The Oracle Control Deck (§1) is shown by default. Select any unsolved puzzle from the dropdown to see its confidence bar and NOVA band hex ranges.
    2
    Use the Orchestration Grid (§3) for batch analysis.
    The §3 sub-panel shows all 77 unsolved puzzles in a sortable table. Click Batch Analyse to compute confidence scores for all puzzles at once. Export as CSV for external comparison.
    3
    Run the xPoint6 Attack Modes (§5) for known-pubkey puzzles.
    §5 exposes 6 algorithm modes targeting puzzles #140, #145, #150, #155, #160: BSGS Bounded · Kangaroo/Pollard · φ-Proximity · ACA Weighted Band · Gradient Walk · Parallel Random. Combined prize: 75.0 BTC.
    4
    Check the Recommendations Engine (§7).
    §7 ranks all 77 unsolved puzzles by a composite score (confidence × pubkey availability × BTC prize weight). Use the top-ranked puzzle as the starting target for focused single-puzzle scanning.
    §2 Star Chart
    400×400 polar canvas — solved-corpus relPos as interactive stars. Click any star to select that puzzle in the Oracle Control Deck.
    §4 KDE Visualiser
    Live bandwidth slider drives Kernel Density Estimation over the 81-corpus. Zone histogram shows probability mass per region.
    §6 Self-Test Suite
    15 assertions: BigInt #66/#130 precision, corpus counts, KS test, KDE density. Runs on ACA tab open.
    📌 NOVA Band: The ACA Oracle uses a 2.17× NOVA band multiplier over the KDE centroid as its primary zone estimate. It is a corpus-derived prior — not a cryptographic shortcut. The same astronomical difficulty applies to all scan methods.
    🔑 KB Intelligence Layer (v2.2.0) Key Browser smart tools panel
    Open the Key Browser tab to access the KB Intelligence panel (🧠 KB Intelligence v2.2.0 · included in v2.3.0). It sits directly above the key table and adds four smart tools — all offline, zero network.
    🔬 Insight Mode
    Toggle [🔬 Insight Mode: OFF → ON]. Every key row immediately expands with a sub-row containing:
    — 32-nibble frequency heatmap: 32 colour bars representing the first 32 nibbles of the key. Green = above-corpus-mean (frequency ratio >1.5×), red = below (<0.5×), grey = near-uniform. Hover any bar for the exact position, nibble value, and frequency ratio.
    — Pattern-score breakdown: relPos · HW · relScore% · hwScore% · nibScore% computed against the learned corpus prior.
    — "How unusual?" verdict: 🟢 Pattern-typical / 🟡 Slightly unusual / 🟠 Unusual / 🔴 Atypical, derived from the composite score.
    ⭐ Strategy Recommender
    Click [⭐ Strategy Recommender] to open a modal with ★1–★5 ratings for all 9 APD strategies, derived from live corpus statistics: relPos σ confidence (learn), χ² bigram significance (markov-nibble), Δ standard deviation (delta-stride), H<2.5 position count (prefix-lock), significant residue count (modular-sieve), corpus size (genetic-sweep), and fixed-prior ratings for entropy-drift, annealing, and auto-learn. The top-rated strategy is pre-selected in the Apply button.
    📈 Pattern Timeline
    Click [📈 Pattern Timeline] to open an SVG chart of all 160 puzzles: green dots show solved keys' actual relPos values; for unsolved puzzles, amber ±1σ and red ±2σ bands show the corpus-predicted relPos range; a dashed green line shows the centroid trend. A visual answer to: "where in each puzzle's range are solved keys historically found?"
    📊 Scan History Overlay
    Click [📊 Scan History Overlay] for a per-strategy breakdown of all keys scanned, wall-clock time, throughput (k/s), and epoch count since the last session start. Coverage meter shows what fraction of a 10M-key budget has been consumed across all strategies.
    [→ Bridge] — Per-Row Strategy Seed
    Every row in the Key Browser table has a small [→ Bridge] button in the rightmost column. Clicking it opens a modal letting you use that key as a seed for any of 4 strategies:
    • 🌡️ Annealing seed — Sets the key as the walk start point, re-heats to T0, and auto-switches to the annealing strategy.
    • 📐 Delta stride origin — Registers the key as the arithmetic base for delta-stride projections.
    • 🧬 Genetic founder — Injects the key into the genetic-sweep population as a founder individual (deduplicated across calls).
    • 🔒 Prefix-lock template — Extracts nibble positions with above-corpus-average frequency from the key, pre-fills the lock table, and auto-switches to the prefix-lock strategy.
    Live feedback appears below the buttons confirming each action.
    🧠 APD Insight Scanning Engine §K 4 corpus-driven scan strategies · §K Auto-Scan · Multi-Hunter
    The APD Insight Scanning Engine promotes APD Insight from a read-only visualiser to a live scanning engine. It contributes four strategies to the main scanner — apd-insight, apd-delta, apd-markov, apd-entropy — each backed by the APD-Learn v2.2.0 corpus. All resolve to segrand in the WASM worker; zone bounds are injected into startHunt() via window._apdZoneOverride.
    1
    Open APD Insight tab and rebuild the corpus.
    Click the 🧠 APD Insight tab. If the corpus summary shows 0 solved entries, click Rebuild. Wait for the summary banner to show relPos centroid and Markov χ² values.
    2
    Use §K Auto-Scan (recommended).
    The §K panel is at the top of the APD Insight tab. Choose an Intelligence Mode (relPos is the most reliable for general scanning; Combined blends all 4 signals). Select a Hunt Scope and Dwell time, then press ▶ Start.
    3
    Or select an APD strategy directly from the main scan panel.
    Open the strategy picker and choose 🧠 APD-Insight, 📐 APD-Delta, 🔗 APD-Markov, or 📊 APD-Entropy. The APD Zone row appears below the strategy picker showing the computed zone bounds and an Apply Zone button to push bounds into Range Min/Max.
    🎯 Single Zone Mode
    Cycles through each unsolved puzzle's corpus zone one at a time. Dwell = time per zone before advancing. Wraps around when queue exhausted.
    ☯ All-77 Multi Mode
    Sets window._apdZoneOverride with per-puzzle zones for all 77 unsolved puzzles. Scanner uses APD zones instead of full puzzle ranges.
    🔑 xpoint6 Pubkey Mode
    Filters to the 5 known-pubkey puzzles (#135–#160). Uses APD zones for them in xpoint mode for maximum speed.
    ⚡ Combined Mode
    Builds 4 batches (one per strategy type) and cycles through them. Covers relPos + delta + Markov + entropy zones in rotation.
    🧠 APD Zone Width Slider: The APD Zone row in the strategy picker shows a Width slider (5–50% of puzzle range, default 10%). Drag it to widen or narrow the corpus zone before pressing Apply Zone or starting §K.
    🧬 PIL v2.3.0 — Puzzle Intelligence Layer DNA zones · Fingerprint clusters · §A Auto-Scan · Multi-Hunter
    PIL derives scan zones from the solved-puzzle corpus using two methods: DNA analysis (bit-probability distribution across solved keys) and Fingerprint clustering (5 density clusters per puzzle). Both power first-class scan strategies (pil-dna, pil-fp) and the §A Auto-Scan zone cycler.
    1
    Select pil-dna or pil-fp from the strategy picker.
    The PIL Zone row appears below the picker showing the computed zone bounds. Press 🎯 Apply Zone to push them into Range Min/Max. For pil-fp, ⏭ Next FP Zone cycles through the 5 fingerprint clusters.
    2
    Use §A Auto-Scan for hands-free zone cycling.
    Open the 🧬 PIL tab. Section A contains the Auto-Scan control panel with mode selector (DNA · FP · Combined), dwell time picker, and Start / Stop / Pause / Skip controls. Zones cycle automatically.
    3
    Multi-Hunter covers all 77 unsolved puzzles or 5 xpoint6 puzzles.
    Select All-77 or xpoint6 scope in §A. PIL builds per-puzzle zone maps and injects them into window._pilZoneOverride so startHunt() uses PIL zones instead of full ranges for every puzzle simultaneously.
    🔗 PIL §K · §F · §P · §S tabs: The PIL tab contains §K DNA Analysis, §F Fingerprint Clusters, §P Pathway Map, and §S Synthesis views for exploring the corpus-derived zones visually.
    ⚙ Settings
    ⚙ Workers & Tuning Presets
    ⚖️ Balanced (Default)
    max(2, CPU_cores−1) workers. Medium batch. All-day scanning without heat or UI jank.
    📱 Mobile-friendly
    2 workers, smaller batch, longer tick. Minimizes heat, extends battery life.
    🖥 Desktop
    CPU_cores−1 workers, larger batch. Best for desktops/laptops on power.
    ⚡ Turbo
    All CPU cores, batch=4096, tightest tick. Uses maximum CPU/RAM. Best for short bursts.
    Workers dropdown: Manual override. More workers = higher throughput up to CPU count. 1 worker for debugging or battery saving.
    Verbose: Detailed TICK/heartbeat/watchdog logging in Activity Log.
    🐶 Watchdog (default ON): Detects stalled workers via heartbeat (3 s interval; declared dead after ~9 s), auto-respawns them. Keep ON for long scans.
    💡 Batch Auto-Tuner: Samples k/s every 5 seconds and adjusts each worker's batch size toward peak throughput — +20% on improvement, −15% on regression (512–65536 bounds). Visible in the Batch stat box.
    📐 Custom Range (Single puzzle mode only)
    Range Min / Range Max inputs accept 64-character hex values defining a sub-range within the puzzle's published bounds. Leave both blank to scan the full range. Out-of-bounds values are automatically clamped (with amber flash animation). All strategies honor the custom range. The Key Browser also jumps to this range for visual inspection.
    ⏳ Auto Background Scan
    Set-and-forget timed scanning. Configure Duration (6 h – 3 months / Until match). The optional 📅 Schedule toggle adds datetime pickers for time-based start/end. Recurrence options: None / Hourly / Daily / Weekly. A match auto-stops the scan and downloads the result. Wake-lock acquisition (where supported) prevents deep sleep during active scans.
    🔧 Advanced Settings (▼ disclosure below tuning row)
    Group 1 — Performance Toggles:
      ☐ SharedArrayBuffer Worker Pool — Opt-in. Zero-copy SAB sharing of H160 prefix set. Requires COOP/COEP headers (not available on most file:// origins).
      ✅ Bloom Filter H160 Prefilter (default ON) — 256 KB 3-hash filter rejects >99.998% of non-matching candidates. Keep ON.

    Group 2 — Coverage & Strategy:
      ✅ Coverage Map — Bitfield persists visited blocks to localStorage. Prevents re-scanning across page reloads.
      ✅ Dynamic Puzzle Weight — Biases random puzzle selection toward under-scanned puzzles (inverse-coverage fairness).
      ✅ Auto-slice range across workers — Partitions puzzle range into N equal sub-ranges for Sequential and Walk strategies.
    🔔 Match Alerts
    1. Enable the 🔔 Alert checkbox on the scan panel (enabled by default as of v1.8.0).
    2. Grant browser notification permission when prompted. If denied, go to browser Settings → Site permissions → Notifications → Allow.
    3. Use the Alert volume slider (0–100%, default 70%) to set chime volume. Preview with the ▶ xpoint or ▶ generic buttons.

    On a match: 3-note ascending chime (Web Audio API) + desktop notification (Browser Notification API) + full-screen found overlay with private key and one-click copy + haptic feedback on mobile.
